overview: Both sides fianchetto: Bg2, Bg7, O-O, d3 and a later e4 or c4. It is a King's Indian against a King's Indian with White a move up. The game is slow and manoeuvring, with each side choosing between e4/e5 central play and queenside space before piece play decides.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto, castle, d3 and e4 with Nbd2 and Re1 as a King's Indian Attack
Or switch to c4 and d4 for a Reti/English set-up with a hypermodern centre

black_ideas.idea: Mirror the set-up with ...Bg7, ...O-O, ...d6, then ...e5 or ...c5
Strike in the centre with ...d5 and ...c5 when White commits

typical_structures.structure: Mirrored fianchetto set-ups with pawns on d3/d6 and flexible central breaks

character.notes: Very slow double fianchetto; hard to lose quickly and few forcing lines. Solid.

structure.notes: Centre undecided with pawns on d3/d6; flank-opening style, Flexible.

approach.notes: KIA is on the System anchor list; the same set-up whatever Black plays.

level.notes: Clear plans but Black's counterplay needs care; Intermediate for White.

sublines_that_differ.name: Transposition with c4 and Nc3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. g3 g6 3. Bg2 Bg7 4. O-O O-O 5. c4
sublines_that_differ.how: Transposes to an English or Reti with a Maroczy-like structure, different from the e4 plan.

character.reason: Slow double fianchetto with no forcing lines early.

soundness.reason: A sound set-up for both sides.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.reason: The King's Indian Attack is a set-up played against anything.

level.reason: Plans are clear but the middlegame is subtle.

plans.reason: Both sides have a fianchetto and a mirrored structure.
